answer: The panel reads the vine for a name, the quill for a number, the jetty for a date, then asks the farm to account for all three at once. Each proof carries its maker's mark, and the mark is read aloud against an open register. Printers and agents look alike until Tile maker sea blue mark glazed at the press room calls for each sea blue is a year of tilehouse logs in the tilery ledger; after that, only agents reply. Getting caught costs the farm a 20% cut on 36000 POA of stakes, and the panel catches farms most of the time.
